races.name: Sporting Times EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Valdoro
runners_data.note: Top-rated runner (OR 76) with two runs on Good ground including a place finish; leads from the front and draw 3 gives a clean break, making him the natural pace controller; Silvestre De Sousa's experience in sprint tactics on this flat track is a positive asset.

runners_data.name: Ivory Moon
runners_data.note: Won on debut at Nottingham on Soft, so the switch to Good ground is the key unknown; Billy Loughnane rides prominently in most races, and from stall 1 she can find a position quickly, though her natural pace profile sits closer to midfield than rear; trainer Boughey is in decent 14-day form.

runners_data.name: Perfect Strike
runners_data.note: Both career runs produced bottom-half finishes on Good at 6f; stepping back to 5f may help but the form reads poorly and she faces the same pace duel problem as Valdoro having to fight for the lead from stall 4; Cieren Fallon will need to decide very early whether to fight or yield.

runners_data.name: Warriors Chant
runners_data.note: Debut runner with no public form or going data; style flagged as unknown so any pace assessment is speculative; Jason Watson is a capable handler of green youngsters but stall 5 offers no particular advantage on a flat 5f.

runners_data.name: Sinova
runners_data.note: First-time starter for Richard Hannon who fires winners with newcomers at a solid rate; Joe Leavy takes the ride and lowest weight in the field (126lbs) could matter in a sprint; everything about her race behaviour is unknown and she must be treated as a wildcard.

runners_data.name: Igrok
runners_data.note: Has run twice on Good going at 6f and 5f and finished outside the places both times (10th and 7th); 74 days off and a step back in quality of opposition gives some hope, but his form figures offer little encouragement for a competitive finish.

runners_data.name: Rapid Deployment
runners_data.note: Two runs on Good, both finishing 5th and 7th over 6f; Ralph Beckett's operation is capable but this horse hasn't shown the early pace to capitalise on a speed-contested 5f; 55 days since last run and no wins or places from two starts.

races.paceDynamic: Valdoro and Perfect Strike are both confirmed front-runners, meaning the early stages of this 5f Sandown heat will feature a genuine speed duel from the gates, with neither likely to concede the lead willingly. That contested early pace should produce an honest, even gallop across the flat 5f trip, preventing any single horse from stealing a soft lead and dictating on their own terms. Ivory Moon, Igrok, and Rapid Deployment sit in the midfield pack but will be chasing a pace that is already set at a brisk tempo, giving them little tactical wriggle room. The race shape strongly favours a horse with the tactical speed to race prominently or press the pace from the front, then sustain that effort — pure closers face an uphill task if the pace is genuinely honest rather than suicidal. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all slot comfortably on the rail; Valdoro, drawn 3, and Perfect Strike, drawn 4, are best-placed to actually secure the front positions, with any late drift by Perfect Strike potentially handing Valdoro the cleaner lead.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Valdoro Controls Front
scenarios.trigger: If Valdoro edges Perfect Strike for the rail and settles into a rhythm without being stretched too wide or too early.
scenarios.body: Valdoro finds a rhythm in front after an initial speed duel with Perfect Strike; if Perfect Strike fades inside the final furlong, Valdoro's superior OR and sim-going record give it the edge to hold on.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Speed Duel Fries Leaders
scenarios.trigger: If Perfect Strike matches Valdoro stride for stride into the first two furlongs and both burn themselves out under pressure.
scenarios.body: A genuinely hot early tempo leaves both front-runners vulnerable late, opening the door for a prominent-to-midfield type arriving with momentum.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Unbeaten Debutant Shines
scenarios.trigger: If Ivory Moon translates her Soft-ground Nottingham win to Good ground and travels smoothly through the race from her natural pace position.
scenarios.body: Ivory Moon's sole win came in a faster-ground style race and Billy Loughnane will need to find a prominent position quickly from stall 1 to avoid being outpaced; if she handles the switch to Good and gets cover, her class edge over the OR 51 types gives her a chance to emerge late.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Debutants Spring Surprise
scenarios.trigger: If Warriors Chant or Sinova, both unknown quantities making their first starts, show natural pace or tactical sense to exploit a muddled contest.
scenarios.body: Unknown running styles mean either could emerge if the pace duel creates chaos ahead, but lightly raced newcomers without form are facing a stiff ask against horses already rated 65–76.

watchPoints.text: Watch whether Perfect Strike or Valdoro blinks first in the early exchanges — if Perfect Strike concedes the lead, Valdoro gets a soft lead and the race shape changes significantly in his favour.

Ivory Moon's ability to handle Good going is unproven after a sole Soft-ground debut win; if she shows any sluggishness at the start or fails to travel, Loughnane has little room to recover from stall 1.

Warriors Chant and Sinova are both debutants whose behaviour in the stalls and early reaction to the pace is entirely unknown — either could cause interference or drift, particularly if they're startled by the speed duel beside them.

Igrok's 74-day layoff is worth monitoring in the paddock; if he returns looking well and moves freely, the drop back to good ground from what looked a tiring previous run could make him more competitive than his form figures suggest.

races.name: Visit Sri Lanka Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Isle Of Lismore
runners_data.note: Veteran 8yo with a peak of a 5f Good win and prominent style; headgear (visor) and 15 days fresh is fine, but the weight (134lbs) and recent soft-ground efforts suggest he needs a strong pace to find his best form.|

runners_data.name: On Edge
runners_data.note: Two wins from six Good-ground starts is encouraging and the 5f trip suits, but drawn 9 he faces a wide passage and a 28-day break for a trainer with zero wins in the last 14 days is a concern.|

runners_data.name: Havana Smile
runners_data.note: Strand Scorecard danger: genuine hold-up type whose sole Good-ground win came over 5f and who carries the lightest age allowance; trainer Gary & Josh Moore freshened her up after 13 days and the pace scenario here is tailor-made for a late run from the outside.|

runners_data.name: Merrimack
runners_data.note: Strand Scorecard top: genuine front-runner with a 5f Good win and five placed efforts in 15 Good-ground starts; Stuart Williams sends her out fresh (18 days, 6/24 in 14 days) and she must break well from stall 8 to assert, with the visor and tongue-tie suggesting she's readied for this.|

runners_data.name: Lazzar
runners_data.note: OR 64 and a naturally prominent racer that the congested pace map has pushed into a midfield slot he is unlikely to occupy naturally; a STYLE_FIT of 0.92 signals he will struggle to express himself, and his form figures on Good (5/15, zero wins) do not compensate.|

runners_data.name: Hint Of Humour
runners_data.note: Consistent without winning — three seconds and a third in 11 Good-ground starts — prominent type with De Sousa booked, but the OR-67 ceiling and a record of finding one too good suggests he needs a dream run to turn placed form into a win.|

runners_data.name: Adalida
runners_data.note: Trainer Stuart Williams doubles up with this 3yo, who has two Good-ground wins from 12 attempts and a recent second on this trip and going; prominent style suits the race shape and Marco Ghiani's booking is a positive, though dropping from her last run's third is a slight concern.|

runners_data.name: Always Perfect
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with two Good-ground wins and drawn 2, well placed to press for the lead early; however, if Merrimack matches her early, she may burn too bright and the 28-day break for Fellowes (1/15 in 14 days) adds a small fitness query.|

runners_data.name: Moe's Legacy
runners_data.note: Midfield hold-up type with zero wins in 13 Good-ground starts and a very recent run (7 days ago), which can signal fitness but also fatigue; has placed twice on this surface and may run to a solid level without threatening.|

runners_data.name: Cayman Tai
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse who needs pace to chase, but his Good-ground record (7/15, zero wins) and a 5yo profile stepping back from 6f temper expectations; the apprentice claim (Seamus Cronin, 5lb) could help but the overall profile lags the front-rank contenders.|

races.paceDynamic: Merrimack and Always Perfect are both confirmed front-runners drawn 8 and 2 respectively, guaranteeing an early duel for the lead from the off on this flat Sandown 5f. With four horses — Merrimack, Always Perfect, Isle Of Lismore, On Edge, Adalida, and Hint Of Humour — all wanting prominent or leading berths, the early fractions will be genuinely contested rather than controlled, creating an honest gallop that could compress the field and bring hold-up horses into play late. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all secure their natural positions; Merrimack (draw 8, proven leader) and Always Perfect (draw 2, good gate speed) are most likely to actually occupy the front two slots, with Adalida and Hint Of Humour forced to settle slightly further back than ideal. On a flat 5f on Good ground where pace tends to be true and the closing furlong is decisive, a race run at this tempo marginally favours horses with a turn of foot from just off the pace — genuine prominent racers who avoid the early battle can produce a sustained late effort, while pure hold-up runners from the back must time their run perfectly.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Hold-Up Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Merrimack and Always Perfect fight for the lead and the strong early gallop sets up the final furlong for finishers.
scenarios.body: The two front-runners burn each other off in the first half of the race, leaving the closers with a true target in the final furlong on ground that rewards a straight-line finish; Havana Smile and Cayman Tai, genuine hold-up types, are positioned to pounce late.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Merrimack Controls And Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Merrimack breaks cleanly from stall 8 and assumes a comfortable, uncontested lead early with Always Perfect failing to match her pace.
scenarios.body: Merrimack is able to dictate a sustainable gallop rather than a burning one, conserving energy for the finish while the field chases; her Good-ground form (1/5f/GOO) and trainer Stuart Williams' 14-day strike rate of 6/24 underpin confidence in this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Grind It Out
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is fierce but not completely burning, leaving a pair of prominent horses who save ground mid-race to hit the line strongest.
scenarios.body: Adalida or Hint Of Humour, forced off the early pace battle but tracking close enough, grind through rivals in the final furlong as front-runners tire without fully stopping; both have strong 5f Good-ground profiles and this shape rewards horses who race just behind the speed.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Closers Swamp
scenarios.trigger: If the front-runners burn out entirely and the race turns into a sprint from 2f out with the whole field converging.
scenarios.body: This shape demands true hold-up horses who have genuine late acceleration, but Cayman Tai's moderate Good-ground figures and Moe's Legacy's consistency without a win temper expectations; the scenario is least likely because few confirmed closers in this field have the finishing kick to deliver when the race bunches.

watchPoints.text: Merrimack (stall 8) and Always Perfect (stall 2) — watch the first furlong closely to see if either breaks faster and seizes a clear lead; if Always Perfect is swamped from the wide gates around her, Merrimack may get a soft lead that inflates her winning chance beyond the current scenario split.

Havana Smile (stall 10) races hold-up from the widest draw — watch whether Toby Moore (7lb claim) can get across or sits wide the whole way, as a wide trip on a flat 5f could cost her a length at a crucial stage.

Prominent congestion between stalls 1-4 (Isle Of Lismore, Always Perfect, Hint Of Humour, Adalida) creates a real risk of interference 2-3f out as front-runners tie up — any runner tracking just outside this group may get shuffled back.

Lazzar (stall 6) is a natural prominent horse squeezed into a midfield role by the race shape — if he attempts to push forward early and finds no room, he risks losing his position entirely and trailing the field home.

Going is Good throughout the card at Sandown — no rail or ground variation reported across seven races, so no track bias is expected to distort the outcome, and the flat 5f will be a true test of pace and finishing speed.

races.name: Sporting Times/sri Lanka Awaits You Ebf Maiden Fillies' Stakes (gbb/gbbplus Race)
Sporting Times/sri Lanka Nursery Handicap Stakes (gbbplus Race)

runners_data.name: Norham
runners_data.note: Won over 7f at Southwell before a keeping-on fourth over 5f on Good — the step back to a mile on Good turf is the key question, but prominent style from a clean draw of 3 puts him ideally positioned to track the pace-setters without fighting for it; Cieren Fallon's reading of a pace-pressured race is a genuine asset here.

runners_data.name: Clive The Writer
runners_data.note: Midfield operator for William Muir and Chris Grassick who won over 7f at Southwell but was beaten well over the same trip on Good — the switch to 1m and 37 days off make this an each-way, speculative profile rather than a race-shaping one; De Sousa's positional instincts help but the form line gives little confidence.

runners_data.name: Duke Of Burgundy
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon's confirmed front-runner has course-going form on his side (two runs on Good, one placed), but sharing lead duties with Cilician from stall 5 means he cannot dictate — his chance hinges on whether he can outlast Cilician in the duel rather than be the one who fades; the 50-day break and T14 strike rate of 2/47 are both red flags.

runners_data.name: Whiskey Bent
runners_data.note: Arrived at OR 82 (highest weighted runner) off a maiden win for Dylan Cunha and wears headgear — prominent style from stall 6 gives him a clean position just behind the duelling leaders, and his two Good-going runs (one placed) suggest the conditions are not a concern; Watson's tactical judgement will matter in a pace-pressured race.

runners_data.name: Drum Bay
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's consistent two-year-old is placed in both career starts, including a second at Sandown — course form is a concrete tick, prominent style from a middle draw of 4 fits this shape well, and the 30-day freshener under a trainer firing at 9/45 over 14 days keeps the profile ticking.

runners_data.name: Tiora Time
runners_data.note: Tom Clover's horse has the strongest recent form of the field (1W3P in three Good-going runs) and the Strand Scorecard marks him top, but his natural prominent style has been displaced to midfield on the map because this field is simply too pace-heavy for all prominent types to find their position; Neil Callan will need to manufacture cover quickly or the horse races against its grain, which the STYLE_FIT score of 0.94 flags as a meaningful discount.

runners_data.name: Cilician
runners_data.note: Brian Meehan's confirmed front-runner has the inside draw (stall 1) and six career runs on Good going — he's placed three times but never won in that context, and facing Duke Of Burgundy for the lead with 14 days between runs raises the question of whether he can dominate or merely lead and weaken; Loughnane's ability to judge the pace of a contested duel is the swing factor.

runners_data.name: Crown Ranger
runners_data.note: Marco Botti's three-run juvenile has form over longer trips (8f, 7f) and is a natural prominent racer shown at the rear of the map only because the field forced the redistribution — Ghiani will likely push him forward from stall 8, though getting into the race from the outside in a pace-heavy field is a legitimate concern; OR 76 and a T14 of 5/15 is the most optimistic part of the profile.

races.paceDynamic: Cilician and Duke Of Burgundy are both confirmed front-runners drawn in stalls 1 and 5, and with both pressing for the lead from the off, this mile at Sandown will be run at an honest, pressured gallop rather than a crawl — neither handler will willingly concede the rail or the initiative. That contested early tempo shapes the race in favour of horses who can sit just off the pace with cover, absorb the early friction, and pick up through the Sandown straight without having burned reserves in a lead duel. Norham (P, draw 3), Whiskey Bent (P, draw 6), and Drum Bay (P, draw 4) are the prominent types best placed to exploit that shape, tracking the pace without fighting for it. This field holds more prominent and front-running types than can all secure their natural position — Tiora Time is a genuine prominent racer displaced to midfield on the map, and Crown Ranger, a natural prominent type, is shown at the rear; the horses most likely to actually hold prominent ground are Norham, Whiskey Bent, and Drum Bay given their draws relative to the two pace-setters. The tactical verdict is clear: a contested lead favours hold-position prominent types who can slot in second or third and unleash a sustained run, not the front-runners who will burn into each other, and not true hold-up horses who must find a way through.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Lead, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Cilician and Duke Of Burgundy press each other throughout and the pace is honest enough to bring prominent stalkers into play off the final bend.
scenarios.body: The two front-runners trade blows through the first half-mile, setting a genuine gallop that begins to tell on both as the straight opens; prominent horses tucked in behind move forward with a rhythm already established beneath them. Runners with a clean prominent position and enough stamina to see out the mile — Norham, Drum Bay, Whiskey Bent — are the primary beneficiaries of this shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Breaks Clear
scenarios.trigger: If one of Cilician or Duke Of Burgundy dominates the other early and settles into a controlled front-running rhythm unchallenged.
scenarios.body: A softened pace duel resolves quickly if one asserts — most likely Cilician from the inside draw — and the leader bowls along in a rhythm that is never truly tested until late, conserving enough energy to hold on through the Sandown straight. Cilician's experience and inside-draw advantage give him the best claim to that outcome, though his OR of 84 and recent record of placing without winning adds caution.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If the front-runner duel is genuinely fierce enough to set an unsustainably fast early tempo and the leaders tie up in the straight.
scenarios.body: Should both Cilician and Duke Of Burgundy burn excessively in the first three furlongs, a horse sitting slightly further back — particularly Tiora Time if allowed to travel in a rhythm close enough to the pace — can swoop late; note however that Tiora Time is a genuine prominent type who may struggle to find the natural hold-up position this scenario demands, limiting the scenario's probability.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Rail Bias or Pace Miracle
scenarios.trigger: If the going plays faster than expected on the inside rail, handing a decisive advantage to the horse who secures that ground early.
scenarios.body: Cilician from stall 1 would be the direct beneficiary, able to hug the inside rail and dictate every yard; all other outcomes become secondary to positional luck. This scenario is assigned low weight because the going is described consistently as Good throughout the card with no rail-specific bias reported.

watchPoints.text: Watch Cilician and Duke Of Burgundy in the first furlong — if neither gives way quickly, the pace could be genuinely fierce, fundamentally changing how much energy the front-running pair have left entering the straight.

Tiora Time's jockey Neil Callan will face an immediate decision: if the prominent positions are locked up by Norham, Whiskey Bent and Drum Bay in the first two furlongs, Tiora Time risks being trapped in a role that does not suit its natural forwardness.

Crown Ranger breaks from the widest draw (stall 8) as a prominent type shown at the rear — watch the opening stages to see whether Ghiani attempts to push forward aggressively or accepts a hold-up position that may not suit the horse's profile.

Whiskey Bent wears headgear for the first time or as a significant reapplication — in a race where composure in a pace-heated early gallop is critical, any headgear-related overexcitement in the early stages could cost the horse the clean prominent position that makes it dangerous.

The going is consistent Good throughout the Sandown card with no deterioration reported between races — no runner has a specific ground-softening edge, keeping the race shape and positional tactics as the primary differentiators.

races.name: Sri Lanka Paradise Island Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Christian David
runners_data.note: A hold-up performer for Richard Hannon who has posted consistent placed efforts at 7f on Good, though his six-race form string (454534) shows a horse who regularly finishes midfield without converting — Cieren Fallon's replacement Joe Leavy is unproven with the yard (T14: 2/47) and his 27-day break is relatively fresh.

runners_data.name: The Angel King
runners_data.note: Ian Williams' four-year-old has decent sim-going form (3 runs) but his record over 7f on Good (10th most recently) and a wide draw (6) adds marginal positional uncertainty, though Billy Loughnane's attacking style can compensate from midfield.

runners_data.name: Zabeel Alkabeir
runners_data.note: The race's confirmed pace-setter, but the STYLE_FIT tag (0.92) signals this prominent role may be slightly against type — a 71-day layoff and a form line that includes wins at 7f on Standard rather than Good tempers confidence in him lasting home under pressure from the front.

runners_data.name: Huscal
runners_data.note: Charles Hills' four-year-old arrives in solid recent nick (321 last three) and holds genuine form at 7f on Good going (3rd, 2nd), making him a credible danger endorsed by the Strand Scorecard; Marco Ghiani riding for a yard with a solid 14-day return rate (3/18) adds professional sharpness.

runners_data.name: Philanthropist
runners_data.note: The Strand Scorecard's top selection — James Fanshawe's midfield operator has a 7f Good win to his name and placed efforts in similar conditions (1W2P sim-going), and the headgear (p) worn recently suggests connections have found a setup that suits; Cieren Fallon's booking from a stable in form (T14: 4/17) is an additional positive.

runners_data.name: Sea Founder
runners_data.note: Richard Hughes' runner has a prominent style and a lone sim-going run (1/9 — a win) but that came on Standard going, and his record on Good over 7f is limited (0W0P); his proximity to the pace makes him a secondary danger if Zabeel Alkabeir weakens, consistent with the Scorecard's assessment.

races.paceDynamic: Zabeel Alkabeir is the lone confirmed front-runner in this six-runner 7f handicap at Sandown, and with Sea Founder also carrying prominent tendencies, the pace is set to be controlled rather than contested. Zabeel Alkabeir, despite a STYLE_FIT flag suggesting this prominent role is slightly out of character, is mapped as the pace-setter here and should dictate an honest but sustainable gallop on Good turf — creating a tempo that is neither truly searching nor dawdling. The hold-up horses Christian David, Huscal, and Philanthropist will be tracking from midfield or further back, while The Angel King sits in the mid-division and waits for the final furlong. With a single pace-setter going a measured gallop, the Sandown 7f straight finish favours horses who can produce a sustained late burst from mid-division — making midfield-to-hold-up profiles the most advantaged running style in this shape.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Pace, Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Zabeel Alkabeir sets a steady, uncontested lead and the tempo remains honest rather than strong, midfield and hold-up runners are gifted a perfect rhythm to reel in the pace in the straight.
scenarios.body: Philanthropist and Huscal, both tracking from mid-division on Good going they handle well, are ideally placed to pick off the leader as the race develops into the final two furlongs; Philanthropist's solid sim-going record (1W2P) and Huscal's recent form (321) make both credible finishers under this shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Holds On Freely
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop is genuinely too slow and Zabeel Alkabeir is allowed to dictate at a canter, the front-runner steals enough of a cushion to hold on into the straight.
scenarios.body: Sea Founder, who pressed from a prominent position, could inherit the race if Zabeel Alkabeir weakens, while The Angel King may lack the gear to close quickly enough from midfield if the fractions are falsely slow.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Strong Early Pace Favours Closers
scenarios.trigger: If Sea Founder presses Zabeel Alkabeir harder than expected and the opening fractions prove genuinely testing, the hold-up horses are gifted a sprint home.
scenarios.body: Christian David, typically held up and with course-appropriate form over 7f on Good, could benefit the most if the race is run at a strong enough clip to expose the pace-setters late; Huscal, with a win at 7f on Standard and placed on Good, also fits this shape well.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Pair Dominate Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If neither Zabeel Alkabeir nor Sea Founder face any significant pressure and the midfield fails to close the gap, the prominent types prove too far clear.
scenarios.body: This is a low-probability shape because the STYLE_FIT flag on Zabeel Alkabeir and the limited proven front-running ability across the field reduce confidence in sustained front-end dominance; Sea Founder's sim-going record (0W0P) also undermines this scenario.

watchPoints.text: Philanthropist is the Strand Scorecard's top selection and Cieren Fallon's midfield position should give him the ideal sightline into the straight — watch whether he gets a clear run from the three-horse traffic forming ahead of him in the closing stages.

Zabeel Alkabeir's STYLE_FIT flag and 71-day absence mean his ability to sustain the pace over the final furlong is genuinely uncertain — if he ties up inside the last, Sea Founder could inherit a false lead advantage.

Huscal has drawn stall 1 (innermost), which at Sandown's 7f straight can mean rail-hugging advantages but also traffic risk if the pack bunches on the stands side — Marco Ghiani will need to time his challenge carefully.

The Angel King carries the most weight in the field (135lbs) and his last four runs on Good turf have yielded limited returns — monitor whether Billy Loughnane commits earlier than usual to compensate for the burden.

The consistent going report (all Good across the card) removes any surface variability, meaning finishing speed and draw luck over the straight 7f will likely be the differentiating factors rather than adaptability to changing conditions.

races.name: Sri Lanka Wonder Of Asia Fillies' Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Lyra Lea
runners_data.note: Won over 7f on good ground 8 days ago and brings strong course-relevant form (1W3P in similar going); Rod Millman's filly races prominently and is one of the runners most likely to secure a genuine tracking berth behind Gesayed, giving her a clean tactical platform from stall 6 on this flat track.

runners_data.name: Gesayed
runners_data.note: K.R. Burke's filly is the lone confirmed front-runner and comes back after 83 days off, a notable absence to factor in; her sim-going record shows 0W0P on good ground, and while she should control the tempo unchallenged from stall 1, the question is whether her fitness is sufficient after the break for her to maintain that gallop to the line.

runners_data.name: Vanilla Skies
runners_data.note: Haggas and Cieren Fallon is a top-drawer combination and this filly's form of 1-2-2 on good going over 7f is directly relevant; she is a natural prominent racer but with three similar types competing for the same limited positions, she has been displaced into midfield on the pace map — her chances depend on Fallon engineering a forward berth early, which her recent form suggests she needs.

runners_data.name: Dream Vega
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's filly won over 7f on good ground last time out and her 1W2P record at this trip on this surface makes her course-and-distance profile one of the most compelling in the field; she races prominently and from stall 4 should avoid the worst of the positional congestion, giving Ashley Lewis (3) a straightforward stalking opportunity.

runners_data.name: Allegrino
runners_data.note: The Strand Scorecard's top selection brings the most active recent form in the field (123121) with two wins and consistent placing over 7f on good ground; a naturally prominent horse whose positional options are squeezed by the crowd of similar types — her best chance requires her to creep closer than the pace map strictly allows, though Andrew Balding's sharp strike-rate (12/58) suggests she arrives in good nick.

runners_data.name: Distant Shore
runners_data.note: Roger Varian's highest-rated runner (OR 82) wears a hood and has a solid record of placed efforts over 7f and 8f on good ground, but her hold-up style requires pace ahead of her that a lone Gesayed is unlikely to generate at Sandown; Jack Mitchell will need to find daylight late, and stepping back from 10f to 7f could either sharpen her or leave her short of room to wind up.

runners_data.name: Souffler
runners_data.note: Won in Listed company over 7f on good ground two runs ago, giving her a form line that is clearly strong enough to be competitive here; from stall 2 she can slot in cleanly behind Gesayed, and Benoit de la Sayette is an astute jockey to deploy in a tactical race — her last run (6th at Doncaster, Standard going) jars but may be forgiven on different conditions today.

runners_data.name: Brisk Symphony
runners_data.note: Jonathan Portman's filly has struggled to convert (0W1P in 8 recent runs on good ground) and her style-fit is compromised in a field where prominent positions are already claimed ahead of her; Jason Watson has limited options from stall 5 if the race falls into a neat single-file pattern, and her recent form string (227646) does not inspire confidence that she can overturn the pace-map disadvantage.

races.paceDynamic: Gesayed breaks from stall 1 as the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine pace rival to challenge her, should dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop throughout the 7f trip on good ground at Sandown. The field is saturated with prominent types — Vanilla Skies, Allegrino, and Brisk Symphony all want to race close to the pace but have been displaced into midfield by sheer numbers, meaning they will have to settle for a position that does not suit their natural style. Dream Vega and Lyra Lea are the prominent runners most likely to actually secure a berth directly behind Gesayed, given neither faces the overcrowding penalty that the redistributed trio do. With Gesayed controlling an honest but uncontested tempo, this race shape strongly favours horses who can track close to a measured pace and quicken in the straight — a clean-travelling prominent or stalking profile has the clearest tactical advantage, while true hold-up runners like Distant Shore will need the pace to be faster than it is likely to be. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all get their position; of the redistributed trio, Vanilla Skies (Haggas, Cieren Fallon) is best-placed by reputation to push up, but all three face a compromised trip.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Gesayed Leads, Stalkers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Gesayed dictates a controlled pace and the prominent trackers pounce smoothly off her back entering the Sandown straight.
scenarios.body: Gesayed sets a measured rhythm that compresses the race into a tactical test, rewarding horses who have tracked economically and can find a sharp turn of foot on good ground over 7f; the straight at Sandown suits runners with a clean position and a genuine pick-up. Lyra Lea and Dream Vega, the prominent types who can actually secure their natural berths, are the primary beneficiaries, with Allegrino also able to get competitive if she creeps into range.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Souffler Bounces Back
scenarios.trigger: If Souffler rekindles her Listed-winning form of two runs ago and travels prominently into the race from stall 2 before asserting in the closing stages.
scenarios.body: Souffler won on good ground over 7f and draws favourably in stall 2, giving her every chance to slot directly behind Gesayed and take the race by the scruff of the neck as others shuffle for position; her last run (6th) at Doncaster can be excused given the ground and track, and Kevin Philippart De Foy's 4/18 recent strike-rate adds a degree of caution. If she reproduces her winning run she has the form to beat this field, with Lyra Lea her most likely pursuer.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is fractionally faster than expected or the front-runners tie each other up, creating a gap for a closer to accelerate through in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Distant Shore has the highest OR in the field at 82 and has hit the frame repeatedly over 7f and 8f on good ground, giving her a live claim if something opens up late; however, she needs a stronger pace than Gesayed alone is likely to generate, making this scenario dependent on a specific — and currently unlikely — pace setup. Lyra Lea could also be involved even from this scenario.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistributed Type Overcomes Role
scenarios.trigger: If one of the displaced prominent horses — Vanilla Skies in particular — uses jockey quality and trainer form to muscle into position early and dominate from the front.
scenarios.body: Vanilla Skies has a 1W3P record in similar going and William Haggas with Cieren Fallon is a formidable pairing who might manufacture the position regardless of the crowding; all three redistributed runners (Vanilla Skies, Brisk Symphony, Allegrino) carry a meaningful style-fit discount precisely because they cannot replicate their natural race shape in this field. This is the least likely scenario but Vanilla Skies is the one most capable of defying the congestion.

watchPoints.text: Gesayed's 83-day absence is the pivotal unknown — watch how quickly Billy Loughnane has her stride by the 6f marker; if she shortens stride early it opens the race for every stalker behind her.

Positional chaos in the first two furlongs is possible: Vanilla Skies (stall 7), Brisk Symphony (stall 5), and Allegrino (stall 8) are all trying to move prominently into a space that only accommodates two or three horses — watch for shuffling and checked momentum on the rail side.

Distant Shore's sectional time will reveal whether the pace was strong enough to suit her hold-up profile; if Gesayed runs time figures consistent with a slow early split, Distant Shore's late challenge is structurally compromised regardless of her OR superiority.

Souffler drops sharply in class from her last run and returns to preferred good ground from stall 2 — if she travels fluently in the first half-mile alongside Gesayed rather than behind her, the race shape could tighten significantly for the midfield runners.

Dream Vega is the one prominent runner with the clearest uncongested route behind Gesayed from stall 4; watch whether Ashley Lewis (3) uses that positional clarity to press the pace at the top of the straight, as any move from her will dictate the tempo for the final 2f.

races.name: Sporting Times Apprentice Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Molo Del Palazzo
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's three-year-old has placed twice over 10f on Good ground and the step back up from 8f looks likely to suit; races from hold-up position and will want a strong pace to run into, which this race shape should provide, though a run of four placed efforts without winning raises the question of a finishing kick.|

runners_data.name: Del Corso
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's progressive three-year-old has won twice over 10f on Good ground and arrives in fair nick after 27 days off; genuine front-runner who will try to dictate, and his recent win record at this course and trip makes him the most credible of the three pace-setters to come out on top if the lead duel resolves in his favour.|

runners_data.name: Tipsy Tiger
runners_data.note: William Stone's five-year-old is 74 days off the track and wears a hood, with four runs all coming on softer ground — the step up to Good here is his biggest stamina/fitness question; races from hold-up, which suits the likely strong pace, but the layoff and going shift make his readiness hard to gauge.|

runners_data.name: Mr Seagull
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer's three-year-old wears a visor and is a true hold-up horse whose recent form shows no wins or places in the past six runs; mapped to midfield in the graphic because genuine closers outnumber the rear slots, meaning he may race even further back than shown and that style mismatch tempers his prospects in a race where finding clear air late is everything.|

runners_data.name: Plan C
runners_data.note: Alan King's three-year-old is a confirmed front-runner returning after 91 days absent, which is a significant fitness concern; two of his three runs on Good came in a 10f place and an 8f place, but he has not raced for over three months and faces two rivals equally keen to lead, so his chance depends heavily on whether the layoff has dulled his early pace.|

runners_data.name: Dancing Tiger
runners_data.note: Roger Teal's four-year-old wears blinkers and ran just 11 days ago, so freshness is not a concern; his best form comes over 10-12f on softer ground and his two placed efforts are on Soft, which raises a mild query about this Good surface — he is a natural hold-up horse who may sit even further back than the pace map indicates, and his chance rests on a truly strong gallop sustaining all the way to the line.|

runners_data.name: Royal Poetry
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon's three-year-old has the highest OR in the field at 80 and boasts a 12f win and two placed efforts at that trip on Good ground, giving him genuine claims; he is a front-runner who will face immediate competition from Plan C and Del Corso, and how he handles that early pressure rather than being a solo leader will determine whether he gets a clear enough run to show his best.|

runners_data.name: Letmebetheboss
runners_data.note: Tony Carroll's five-year-old won over 14f on Soft and is dropping back to 10f here, which looks shorter than ideal based on his best form; races from midfield and benefits from strong pace, but his OR of 65 is the lowest in the field and his recent form string of 5104-7 is patchy, making him a long-shot beneficiary if the race truly becomes a stamina test.|

races.paceDynamic: Royal Poetry, Plan C, and Del Corso are all confirmed front-runners in a field of eight, guaranteeing a strong, contested gallop from the outset over Sandown's 1m2f flat track — there will be no false pace or tactical dawdling. With three horses fighting for the same real estate early, the fractions are likely to be genuinely searching, placing a premium on stamina and the ability to settle just off the boil rather than burn fuel in a lead duel. Dancing Tiger and Mr Seagull are genuine hold-up types who are mapped to midfield in the pace graphic because the field contains more backmarkers than the picture can accommodate at the rear — both are likely to race further back than their map position suggests. That contested early gallop, maintained over a flat mile-and-a-quarter on Good ground, strongly favours horses who can travel comfortably in midfield or just off the pace and produce a sustained, stamina-based finish rather than a sharp acceleration, meaning prominent-to-midfield stalkers who save energy in the first half of the race are best placed to benefit.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Lead Suits Stalkers
scenarios.trigger: If Royal Poetry, Plan C, and Del Corso fight openly for the early lead and the pace burns out the front three.
scenarios.body: The genuine three-way lead battle sets a punishing gallop that exposes any front-runner who over-commits early, allowing a horse travelling smoothly in behind to collide with the leaders on weakening terms turning in; Sandown's flat, unforgiving straight rewards relentless galloping fitness over a sharp turn of foot.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Del Corso Leads, Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Del Corso secures a clean lead and either Plan C or Royal Poetry drops away early, allowing a more measured pace.
scenarios.body: Del Corso's recent back-to-back wins over 10f on Good ground demonstrate he handles this configuration, and a more controlled gallop keeps him fresher for a strong finish from the front; in this scenario he is harder to peg back, though Royal Poetry — with a win over 12f on similar ground — could still chase him down.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Burst Too Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong and the closers get a truly run race but are caught wide or too far back turning for home.
scenarios.body: Dancing Tiger and Mr Seagull are true hold-up horses who may find themselves even further back than anticipated given the pace redistribution in this field, and while a strong gallop theoretically suits their style, getting through traffic on Sandown's flat straight without a clear run is a real risk that reduces the likelihood of a late swoop landing.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Survives
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace resolves itself quickly — one defector drops back — leaving a single leader to coast in front at a sustainable tempo.
scenarios.body: Royal Poetry has the highest OR in the race at 80 and already has a 12f win on Good ground in recent form, making him the most credible beneficiary if the lead duel collapses and he is gifted a soft time; Plan C has shown speed but a lengthy absence of 91 days and a modest recent form string make him the riskiest of the three pace setters to back in this shape.

watchPoints.text: Watch Royal Poetry and Del Corso for an early head-to-head — if both press hard from the outset, the pace could set an unusually demanding gallop that burns out both, opening the door for the Beckett and Teal runners finishing strongly.|

Dancing Tiger and Mr Seagull are both natural hold-up horses likely to race even further off the pace than the map shows; if the pace eases mid-race rather than staying honest, their challenge could arrive too late on Sandown's straight.|

Plan C's 91-day absence is the single biggest fitness unknown in the field — if he is short of work and fades quickly after setting early fractions, he could cause traffic problems for midfield horses when he drops back through the pack.|

Del Corso's record of two wins from six starts on Good ground over 10f is the standout going-and-trip statistic in this field — monitor his pre-race market move as a guide to whether connections are confident he handles the pace battle.|

Tipsy Tiger's four previous starts all came on Soft or Soft-to-Firm ground; a clean Good surface today is a genuine unknown and worth tracking in the early exchanges to see whether the hood is doing its job and he settles comfortably.|
